title: Designing and Evaluating Adapted Exercise and Sport Interventions: Toward a Pragmatic, Standardized, and Scalable Framework for Clinical and Community Practice
content: Adapted exercise and sport are increasingly prescribed across clinical, community, and inclusive settings, yet persistent heterogeneity in intervention design, reporting, and evaluation limits replication and large-scale implementation. This methodological paper introduces a pragmatic, standardized, and scalable framework that unifies the full intervention cycle, from risk screening and functional/psychosocial assessment to individualized prescription (FITT-VP), supervision and monitoring, outcome tracking, and reporting/knowledge translation. The framework specifies a core assessment battery (e.g., 6MWT, TUG, 30-s Chair Stand, handgrip; PROMs such as FACIT-F, FACT-G/EORTC QLQ-C30, HADS), operational rules for dose, intensity, and progression across aerobic, resistance, balance/mobility, and mind–body modalities, and decision thresholds based on MCIDs, safety triggers, and adherence milestones. A core outcome set covers functional, clinical, and psychosocial domains, complemented by process indicators (adherence, fidelity, adverse events) and implementation metrics (reach, adoption, feasibility, cost, maintenance). Illustrative use-cases in oncology, metabolic/cardiovascular disease, chronic respiratory conditions, and neurological disorders show how stratification rules, modality mix, and monitoring intensity are tailored across populations, including progression to adapted and inclusive sport. By merging exercise science with implementation frameworks (RE-AIM, TIDieR, CERT) in a single, reusable pipeline, the model strengthens transparency, reproducibility, and person-centered delivery, while creating a practical learning system (routine capture of dose, adherence, adverse events, reach/adoption) for continuous improvement and multi-site synthesis. Overall, it offers a deployable blueprint for clinicians, kinesiologists, researchers, and decision-makers to design, monitor, and report adapted exercise and sport programs with greater fidelity, comparability, and policy relevance.
